one_star_reviews.text:
Dismal experience at Cafe Pans.

The service was lacklustre, disinterested and painfully slow. The staff could barely muster a smile, and unfortunately the service from the female chef was even worse.

Despite ordering relatively simple food, we waited around 15 minutes for the first items — the onion rings and chicken strips — to arrive. The female chef had apparently forgotten our order of chips with bacon and cheese sauce altogether, so these arrived even later. When the chips eventually appeared, they were stone cold. By that stage, after such an extraordinarily long wait, we simply had no option but to eat them.

The onion rings were equally miserable. For around €5, three of the four rings we received were absolutely tiny (about an inch in diameter with no onion), with only one being a modest size. Just as we finished eating, we noticed another customer being served onion rings that looked completely different: four large, crispy rings, each several times the size of ours.

We raised this with the gentleman at the till, who spoke to the inept female chef. Their response, in essence, was that it was simply tough luck. No apology, no attempt to rectify it, and no interest..

Well done, guys. I hope you enjoy your jobs, because bringing any satisfaction to your customers certainly doesn’t appear to be part of them.

You may want to look at both the quality and consistency of the food you are serving, but above all at the attitude towards customers when something clearly isn’t right. Mistakes happen in any restaurant; what distinguishes good service is how staff respond when they do. On this occasion, the response was as depressing as the staff.

one_star_reviews.text: It was a disaster. They performed the installation, but the unit didn't work. The technician who came started dismantling parts of a brand-new appliance worth over €1,000. When it was supposedly working, he left, but the bypass circuit was closed, meaning the water wasn't passing through the water softener. Luckily, I noticed and fixed it. Two weeks later, while testing the water hardness, I discovered the softener wasn't working correctly. I contacted the company, and they said a technician would come to my house. When he finished and performed another hardness test, the unit was working fine, and they charged us €40 without providing an invoice. I wasn't home, and he gave my wife the runaround. It was like those guys who come to your house to replace a gas hose—very strange indeed. I don't have any receipts for the installation work, nor for the work done the following visit. When I told them the device wasn't filtering limescale properly and they said a technician would come, they never mentioned they would charge me. The logical and reasonable thing to do is that if the device is only two weeks old and hasn't been working properly since it was installed, they should take responsibility for the problem and not try to charge me for a job that was done incorrectly from the start. Well, a month later I noticed the water tasted salty; in other words, saltwater was getting into the drinking water system. I contacted them again, and they said they might charge me or not—I have the WhatsApp conversation—and I told them the device had been malfunctioning since day one, that the technician who installed it wasn't very clear on how to use it, and in the end, they referred me to the manufacturer's technical support and washed their hands of the whole thing. They weren't the ones who sold or installed the device, but they were the ones who set it up, and they didn't do it properly. It's probably just a matter of adjusting some parameters, as they told me on WhatsApp, but even knowing it's likely a configuration issue because the technician didn't do it correctly, they're referring me to the service center. So here I am, requesting that the manufacturer check the equipment under warranty, since they won't take responsibility, and given the circumstances, it's better to have a qualified technician come and know what to do.

one_star_reviews.text:
Trapped in Cabin 32,000 Feet Above: My Transavia Nightmare
I still can’t shake the claustrophobia, nor the sheer disbelief of it all. If you had told me before boarding that flight from Palma to Amsterdam that a budget airline could actively make you feel like an intruder in your own seat, I wouldn't have believed you. But Transavia managed it with flying colors.
From the very first moment we stepped onto the plane, it was clear that basic human comfort was an illegal luxury. The seats were jammed together so tightly that our legs had nowhere to go, pinned and crushed against the plastic shells in front of us like a cruel physical penalty for buying a cheap ticket. Every minute in the air felt like a test of endurance.
Yet the cramped quarters were nothing compared to the psychological torture of dealing with the crew. Calling them flight attendants would be an insult to the profession. The women working our aisle weren't hosts or caretakers of the skies; they acted like exhausted wardens managing a restless prison block.
Warmth, empathy, and basic politeness were entirely missing from their vocabulary. Instead, our interactions were reduced to a series of sharp, hostile commands barked down the aisle. We were met with phrases like "It's not my problem," "Stop," "Let me go by," and a harsh, dismissive "Move!" And the absolute pinnacle of absurdity came when one of them snapped at a passenger, glared, and muttered with a straight face, "I’ve never been rude in my life." The lack of self-awareness was suffocating.
By the time we finally touched down in Amsterdam, I wasn't just tired from the cramped travel; I was emotionally exhausted from the pure hostility in the cabin. Flying is already stressful enough without the people responsible for your safety treating you like a miserable nuisance they are forced to babysit.
Horrendous is honestly too light a word for what happened up there. Never, ever again, Transavia.

I'm beyond disappointed! I'm giving it one star because I can't give it less.
They're incredibly incompetent. To begin with, my sister picked up the car, and when she sent me a picture, I saw that each mirror was a different color. Secondly, they left the entire white window seal discolored. They clearly didn't care about getting paint on anything, and they didn't even use the tape that's supposed to prevent staining.
On top of that, the inside of the car was covered in white dust. I couldn't even get the dust off the screen, so I had to spend money to have it cleaned. You don't deliver a car like that! 😡
And what really infuriates me is that when I open the passenger door, I see that paint stain inside the car. Excuse me? That's incredibly unprofessional. Even though it's the only garage in Jerez, I'm not taking it there. I'll go to another city if necessary. I'm extremely careful with my car, and this just isn't right. Why should my car be treated like this? It's truly infuriating.

A young woman opened the door, and I was seen by a Latino man who looked like he'd just woken up, judging by his hair and the way he was rubbing his eyes. He didn't even have his ID with him, so I couldn't see his name. I went into his office, and he immediately addressed me as "ma'am," even though I was a young man, not even 25. Then he told me it was 2:00 AM and that things had to be serious because we were in the emergency department. When I explained why I was there, he bluntly asked me if I hadn't had a month to see my primary care physician, using a dismissive tone and facial expression. He told the nurse to "take his blood pressure," but the nurse didn't seem to understand what he'd asked. Finally, he told me he was going to send me to the hospital or that I could see my primary care physician if I wanted, whichever I preferred. He doesn't prescribe anything for me, and he doesn't even give me a medical report or a referral to the hospital, nor has he offered me transportation or asked if I have a way to get there, telling me to come whenever I want or whenever I can, since, according to him, everything is on the computer. one_star_reviews.text: Less than a month ago, I had to say goodbye to the one who was always more than a dog to me; he was my son. I had to have him euthanized, and the next day he was cremated at this crematorium the veterinary hospital recommended. The disappointment I felt, and the final image, was devastating. To this day, it still weighs heavily on me. They showed me my dog ​​on a metal cart, in front of the oven, positioned terribly, the image completely clumsy—face up, head tilted back so I couldn't even see his face properly—and to top it all off, a small pool of blood coming from his mouth. Don't they realize this? Is this the last image they show someone who is grieving and experiencing loss? I found it unbelievable, incredibly insensitive.

Unfortunately, our pet passed away, and we brought them to this place for cremation. We requested a private service, and the entire process, from when they brought the pet in until they gave us the urn with the ashes, took less than an hour. However, when they gave us the urn, it was the one for another pet, and they told us they had made a mistake and transferred the ashes to a completely different urn. An incredible disappointment. The first and last time.

one_star_reviews.text:
Here's my review after 2 years

This isn't a review written 3 days after the surgery, like they do at this company, where they send you a message asking you to rate them 3 days after the operation. From what I see, 80% of the comments here are exactly that: 3 days after the surgery. And of course, you can only give your opinion if the results are 12 months later... so I wouldn't rely too much on the comments about this company... DON'T FALL FOR IT LIKE I DID!!!!!!!

For an evaluation, they asked me for photos, and based on these, they told me that a hair transplant in the frontal area would be enough, and that the upper area, which was also in bad shape, would only need medication and would grow back thick—basically, I didn't need a transplant.

I purchased the package, exactly as stated on their website, which you can read if you access it: "It was all-inclusive with NO LIMIT ON FOLLICULAR UNITS" <--note

I understand that my head has a limited number of follicular units and that only the maximum number can be extracted, according to what remains in the donor area, so that it doesn't look bad or sparse, and that these can then be placed in the area to be grafted. I know my donor area won't regenerate, but what's there can be extracted in one or two consecutive sessions, not in two separate operations charging double.

On the day of the operation, during an on-site assessment with his magnifying glass, the surgeon told me, and I quote, "THE UPPER AREA IS IN BAD SHAPE AND NEEDS FOLLICLES. I DON'T UNDERSTAND HOW THE OPERATION WAS SCHEDULED FOR JUST ONE DAY. THIS IS A TWO-DAY OPERATION!!"

The operation was then performed, and they grafted hair onto the frontal area and ALSO, minimally, onto the upper area, which, according to them, would improve with medication... implying that the upper area was in bad shape. Excuse me, but if you offer a hair loss treatment and advertise an "ALL-INCLUSIVE, UNLIMITED FOLLICULAR UNITS" package, then I expect you to treat my baldness, not just the frontal area, and leave me with the... Top area, ready paperwork... I hope you'll implant follicles in all areas since I paid for the "ALL-INCLUSIVE UNLIMITED FOLLICULAR UNITS" package. Why do you want to charge me again now if your package is unlimited follicular units? It says so itself, unlimited units... and I'm still bald!

After 12 months of the recovery process, it's clear that the frontal area was bald and the upper area, which would improve with medication, was also bald. Why was the frontal area bald? Because they used the follicles from the frontal area to implant them in the upper area, since physically, there wasn't enough time to do anything else in one day.

Considering that follicles don't grow back, it's clear that the ones extracted in the second operation were available in the first operation. There simply wasn't proper organization when it came to assessing me correctly and implanting them in two sessions.

There More negative comments about Leticap, regarding what "NO LIMIT ON FOLLICULAR UNITS" "REALLY" means to them. It seems to mean they implant the maximum number of units they can in a single day, not the maximum you actually need to achieve a good result and cover your baldness, or what you paid for. I've also read in other replies to negative comments about the same "maximum number of units" policy that they extract as many follicles as the donor area can produce. Of course, if I've had two surgeries and the extracted follicles don't grow back, and hair loses strength and vitality over time, how is it possible that they extracted an additional 2400 units in the second surgery if the donor area was already full? According to them, the time the follicles remain viable after extraction is limited, which is why, as my own surgeon told me, "THIS IS A TWO-DAY OPERATION." They indicate that you need a second operation, which you must pay for, if you really want that "NO LIMIT ON FOLLICULAR UNITS" to apply.

one_star_reviews.text:
Honestly, I didn't want to leave this review, but I feel it's necessary to share my experience, which has been quite negative.

From the first consultation, I felt the assessment wasn't thorough. They didn't use any specialized equipment to examine and clearly document the condition of my scalp, only a small lens attached to a mobile phone. They also didn't take standardized photographs or measurements that would allow for an objective comparison of my progress in subsequent visits.
They recommended a treatment that, in my opinion, was insufficient, along with a series of guidelines that I followed rigorously. After three months, I was still getting worse, although I fully understand that each patient responds differently and that this, in itself, isn't necessarily the professional's responsibility.
I returned for a follow-up appointment and, despite insisting that my case and treatment be reviewed, I continued with practically the same regimen. I also tried treatments at the clinic, including mesotherapy, which were quite expensive and didn't provide any improvement.

In the sixth month, I returned and explained again that I still wasn't seeing any results. I mentioned that I had consulted other professionals and various sources, and asked if the dosages could be reassessed or other options considered. However, no significant changes were made, and my condition continued to worsen.
After nine months of following the recommended instructions and treatments, I reported the situation again. The response was that I had to come in for another evaluation, paying for the consultation again, even though during the previous visits I didn't feel that there had been sufficiently detailed follow-up or an objective comparison of my scalp. Furthermore, at each appointment, I had to explain practically my entire medical history again, as if it were my first time.
I can't get my money or time back, but I'm sharing my experience so that others going through a similar situation can consider different options. My recommendation is to look for a clinic that studies each case individually, documents progress with appropriate resources, reviews the treatment when results aren't achieved, and provides genuine patient follow-up.
This has been solely my personal experience during nine months of treatment.

My experience at this clinic was very negative, and frankly, I left the appointment deeply disappointed.

I went back a year after my previous appointment. During this visit, no physical examination of my scalp was performed, nor was any specific tests or tools used to assess how my condition had progressed since the previous appointment. A detailed review of my medical history was also not conducted to determine my starting point and what changes I might have experienced during that year.

The consultation focused primarily on the fact that, during that time, I hadn't undergone any additional treatments such as mesotherapy or the regenerative treatment that had been previously recommended to me.

Furthermore, I came with some questions related to my treatment. I wanted to ask about issues that other healthcare professionals had raised with me, and specifically, I inquired about the role of minoxidil in my case, as I was unsure why it was considered unnecessary. My intention was simply to understand the reason for the recommendation and to be able to make informed decisions about my treatment.

What I disliked most was the way this part of the consultation unfolded. I felt that my questions and my desire to understand and question certain medical decisions were met with disapproval. Instead of receiving a detailed explanation that addressed my concerns, the conversation ended up focusing on the fact that a year had passed without certain treatments and questioning my reason for returning for another appointment.

At no point did I intend to impose a treatment or question the doctor's professionalism. As a patient, I consider it perfectly legitimate to ask questions, request explanations, and want to know the reasons behind the recommendations I receive.

I left the consultation feeling that I hadn't received the individualized assessment I expected and, above all, with a very unpleasant feeling regarding the way my questions were received.

Of course, this is only my personal experience, and every patient may have a different perception. But, based on my experience, I will not return to this clinic, nor can I recommend it.

one_star_reviews.text:
I went to this clinic for braces on my LOWER teeth. I knew nothing about orthodontics and relied on the clinic to advise me. I was never told that treating only the lower teeth was inappropriate, and Dr. Rojas proceeded to place braces only on my lower teeth.

The following day, I had painful, clearly visible lesions inside my mouth and noticed a dramatic change in my UPPER teeth, which suddenly looked considerably more yellow and dull. I have dated before-and-after photographs documenting these changes. Months later, my teeth still have not returned to how they looked or felt before, and their surfaces remain noticeably rougher to me.

During the procedure, I personally observed an acidic dental product being applied to my upper teeth and areas inside my mouth. The clinic disputes this and has since stated in writing that it was applied only to my lower teeth.

When I returned with my concerns, I found Dr. Rojas dismissive and rude. I was given different possible explanations to what happened, including my dental hygiene and stomach acid. I was initially told I would have to pay for a cleaning/polishing to address the problem. After I said I intended to make an official complaint, it was offered free of charge.

The polishing was extremely painful for me, to the point that I physically stopped the dentist. I documented further wounds and irritation afterwards.

I have submitted an official Hoja de Quejas y Reclamaciones supported by photographic and documentary evidence. The clinic has formally rejected my complaint and denies that its treatment caused the problems I experienced.

I am describing my personal experience and what I documented before and after treatment, rather than making a medical determination about causation.

Months later, my teeth are still not the same. Based on my experience, I would never return.

one_star_reviews.text:
The points in the "Terms and Conditions" section of the Replus website seem outrageous to me. The factory washes its hands of the matter and shirks its responsibility regarding the warranty of the products it manufactures. What happens if the supplier of one of its retail outlets goes bankrupt and disappears? Who honors the warranty on the windows, for example? Can't customers contact another supplier at one of its retail outlets to claim the warranty?
This is something to be wary of.

Pay close attention to point "3. Absence of contractual responsibility" in the Terms and Conditions of use section of the website.

It's a very clever way for REPLUS to evade responsibility, to wash their hands of the matter.

If the company managing one of their "Points of Sale" disappears, or if the end customer loses confidence in that company and doesn't want to deal with them, there's no procedure for enforcing the product warranty.

That's what happened to us. We had all our exterior windows and doors installed by REPLUS, and now we have a problem with one of them. Since we don't trust the company that did the installation, and it has also moved (it's no longer at the REPLUS Point of Sale where we made the purchase), we wanted to resolve the issue with the company that's now at the same Point of Sale, but they tell us it's not possible.

In short, we've been left without the warranty that the windows should have.

If you care about your elderly relatives, I strongly advise you not to be swayed by initial promises. Ask the residents' families, and if even one says they are well cared for at this residence, then make your decision. My mistake was not asking, not reading the reviews, and we have lived through a true nightmare at this residence.
Our case is already under complaint with social services, and I know they will carry out the corresponding inspection. There are countless irregularities: falls that the caregivers denied, asking why they wouldn't change my relative and receiving the answer that my relative urinates a lot, and so on, an endless list of irregularities. We asked for medication and they refused to give it to us, we asked for clothing and when they finally gave us some, they gave us clothes with cigarette holes even though my relative doesn't smoke... and so on, an endless list of irregularities. I repeat, I'm not asking you to take my word for it; ask the residents' families, because I haven't yet found anyone who has described a satisfactory stay.

one_star_reviews.text:
DISGUSTING CORPORATE BEHAV8OUR - THEIR MOBILE PHONE CHARGES ARE A SCAM
When you leave port and lose phone connection, your phone automatically connects to a special 'Maritime GSM' network installed on the ship.
I hadn't bought a wifi package as I was quite happy to not have internet for a few hours. If my phone had connection, great. If not, I'd read my book. A nice idea actually.
I unexpectedly received a text message about high roaming charges and turned my phone off immediately.
This special network connection, which I didn't expect and didn’t agree to, costs about 8 euros per MEGABYTE. No, not 8 euros per gigabyte, per megabyte!
Even though I turned my phone off immediately, they still charged me as my emails must have synced in the background or something.
GNV claim "we are not the company providing the phone service, so it isn't our fault." However, the Maritime GSM company is installed on their ship. They charge the company for having their equipment on board. GNV, you are responsible. I don't care if the ferry is old or runs late, but this business practice is disgusting.

Yes, there were warning signs. I saw two on the entire ship after I went searching. One was facing the wrong way at reception, with another on a wall near the bar. A4 size.
What they do is legal, but absolutely disgusting.
Shame on me for not reading any reviews before booking. It was a day trip on a ferry with my bicycle (also a disappointing experience) and should have been simple.
Shame on you GNV.
PS: I worked 5 years in mobile telecommunications and then 16 years at sea. I still got tricked. What about other guests?

My experience has not been good. I went to a private clinic about a month and a half ago, paying €130, for discomfort in my vulvar area that was causing me considerable pain and burning.

After the evaluation, I was advised to use a cream and an oil. I followed the instructions and bought the recommended products, but after all this time I haven't noticed any improvement and the discomfort continues.

I completely understand that a treatment may not work in all cases, but I expected a more thorough evaluation, follow-up, and, if the initial treatment didn't work, a search for alternatives or a new assessment of the problem.

I left quite disappointed with the care I received and with the feeling that I didn't get a solution to my problem.

one_star_reviews.text:
I asked lawyer Francisco Javier Valverde López-Cañete about receiving a donation from my father in England on June 30, 2026.

On three occasions, during the "interview" and twice in the following weeks via WhatsApp/email, the lawyer insisted that my father—82 years old—would have to travel to Spain to sign the paperwork. I spoke with my brother, and in five minutes he sent me the real information: with the Hague Apostille, my father could sign from England. The Hague Apostille Convention was signed in 1961, 65 years ago! But the lawyer, an expert in inheritance and donations, who charged me €100 for 40 minutes—during which he kept checking his watch—was unaware of its existence, and three months later he still hasn't confirmed this possibility.

I absolutely do not recommend him.

[Postscript: The issue of whether or not my father had to travel was key. I called the lawyer to specifically ask about this point a few weeks after the interview, and he knew nothing about the Hague Apostille. A good person and professional admits their mistakes and apologizes. That's all.]

one_star_reviews.text: This morning the church was open and my partner wanted to show me the little statue I've been in several times without realizing it, which is very famous in Malaga. But I never imagined the behavior of this rude priest who kicked us out of the church, claiming he'd been working all morning and had to close. I hope things go badly for him and that not many people visit the church.

The church was beautiful, but I must emphasize the priest's poor attitude and behavior. He spent the entire ceremony rushing us and trying to finish as quickly as possible, not because we arrived on time, but because he said he had another ceremony. I find this outrageous, especially since two family members were scheduled to read a text that they couldn't. In my opinion, it's shameful to ruin such a beautiful day as a wedding, especially after having booked a specific time. If I had to describe the experience in two words, it would be poor organization.
Every Sunday at 9:00 in the morning the bells ring for 20 minutes….please, we are no longer in the Middle Ages, let us rest.

one_star_reviews.text:
I've been a customer for years, specifically between seven and eight, and my current experience is frankly disappointing.

The service quality is very poor: the Wi-Fi connection is unreliable, the mobile coverage is terrible, and quite frequently the phone loses network access and displays the "emergency calls only" message. What's most worrying is that, when this happens, it's often necessary to restart the device to restore the connection. This isn't an isolated or one-off problem, but rather a situation that occurs far too often and directly impacts a service I'm paying for.

Added to this is the feeling that customer loyalty is completely disregarded. After seven or eight years with the company, no benefits or consideration are offered for long-standing service. Furthermore, when a customer contacts the company to file a complaint or request a solution, the response is equally inadequate.

When I mentioned that most of the reviews I found were negative, the response I received was that this was because people only write reviews to criticize the company, out of boredom, or for similar reasons.

Frankly, I think that explanation is a very inadequate way to deal with criticism. If a large number of customers take the trouble to write a negative review, perhaps the reasonable thing to do isn't to assume they're all doing it "out of boredom," but rather to ask ourselves what's causing that level of dissatisfaction.

A company should use customer reviews to identify problems and improve its service, not simply discredit them. When the same problems keep recurring—poor coverage, connection issues, emergency calls, and customer service that doesn't offer satisfactory solutions—it's hard to believe that all the complaints stem from boredom or a desire to spread discredit.

After so many years as a customer, the least I expect is a stable service, adequate support, and for issues to be taken seriously. Currently, none of those three things are meeting my expectations.

one_star_reviews.text:
I haven't been able to rate the ultrasound service, as my appointment was canceled with less than 24 hours' notice. To be able to attend, I had rearranged my work schedule and taken time off, so this last-minute cancellation meant losing time and having to rearrange my workday.

I fully understand that unforeseen medical issues can arise and that, in this case, it wasn't directly the clinic's responsibility. However, I believe the process could have been handled more professionally. I don't think it's appropriate to communicate the cancellation of an appointment via WhatsApp, especially when it's such an important and delicate appointment as a first ultrasound during pregnancy. I believe that, at the very least, a phone call would have been appropriate to explain the situation personally and offer alternatives over the phone, not through WhatsApp.

I understand that unforeseen events can happen, but patients' time is also valuable: I, too, had to rearrange my work, take time off, and make arrangements to attend. Therefore, I believe that a cancellation with such short notice should be handled with greater consideration for the patient.

I hope you can take this into account for future occasions, because attention and communication in these types of situations are especially important.

A terrible experience with Revuelo. We contacted them through the Digital Kit and they charged €6,000 supposedly to work on three areas (SEO, social media management, and website), which I will now explain:

• Unfinished website: Initially, we had to design and oversee a large part of the website ourselves due to their partner's clear inability to do so. We are almost a year behind schedule with the website's completion, which remains incomplete and full of errors. This is all after hundreds of emails sent for their review (pointing out their errors), dozens of documents with screenshots, months of waiting, and promises of improvements that never materialized. Everything is documented in a nearly 400-page PDF that attests to the process.

• SEO not implemented: The new website is completely devoid of H1 and H2 headings, meta descriptions, images with alt text, keywords, or structured data. This is confirmed by several external audits we have requested.

• Non-existent Social Media: They haven't created a single post on any of our social media platforms during the entire process; in fact, they've never even had access to them. We've been doing it ourselves weekly, supposedly so they'd have more time to dedicate to the website and SEO.

A management style riddled with false promises and a complete lack of professionalism. I've attached screenshots and reports that prove each point.

one_star_reviews.text:
On the 3rd, already at the ticket office of the monastery entrance with our tickets in hand, a man approached us and told us we couldn't enter, that there was an event (a wedding) blocking access. I repeat, with the tickets in hand, purchased just two minutes before. We had to return the tickets, and of course, they refunded our money, but what I'm complaining about is the fact that they could have let us in, even if only to take a look at the cloister. I don't understand the lack of control in ticket sales and not knowing whether or not tickets can be sold if there's an event. The organization was nonexistent, a real shame since we traveled from Madrid for this visit. I don't think I'll try again; it left a very bad taste in my mouth. To top it all off, we went to the Carrión tourist office, and they were unaware of this event at the monastery, even though they had sent other people to do the visit. In short, a disaster. I don't doubt the beauty of the cloister, but unfortunately, we were denied access even with the tickets we had purchased.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with this clinic has been very negative.

The first session was particularly shocking. The consultation began with me, and as I recall, the practitioner spent about 10 minutes with me, glancing at her watch throughout the conversation. Even so, I was charged €100 for myself and another €100 for my 11-year-old son, totaling €200 for that first session.

In those first few minutes, the questions I was asked about my son were mainly basic, such as whether his teeth had come in on time, if he had started walking on time, and if he had started talking on time. I expected a much more in-depth assessment and an initial consultation that was more in line with both the price and the reason for our visit.

Furthermore, we had a recent appointment scheduled for September 21st. Yesterday was Sunday, and I wasn't with my son, so I couldn't know how he was feeling today. When I picked him up from school, I discovered he still had a mouth infection, an abscess, and discomfort from a tooth extraction, so I had to cancel his appointment to have him evaluated.

I understand that a dental practice may have a cancellation policy, but I believe that a medical situation I couldn't have known or foreseen the day before should be treated as an exceptional circumstance. However, I was told that I had to pay for the canceled session and, in addition, I would have to pay for the next appointment.

I have finally decided that my son will not continue with this practice. I have requested the invoices for the sessions I paid for and will pay for today's session, but I feel it's important to share my experience so that other families know what happened to me.

I don't question that each professional has their own way of working, but considering the price I paid, the time spent, and how this last situation was handled, my experience has not met my expectations.

What's hardest to understand is how there can be parents who constantly talk about God, Christian values, love, and the importance of family, and who even hold positions of responsibility within a church, but then, in their own lives, fail to do the most basic thing: act as parents and fulfill their responsibilities to their children.

Because being a father isn't about putting on a show in front of a community, going to church, or talking about God. Being a father is demonstrated by being present, caring for your children, fulfilling your obligations, offering support, and responding when they are truly needed.

It's very easy to talk about love, family, and values ​​in front of others. What's truly important is demonstrating it when no one is watching, especially within your own home and with your own children.

And frankly, it's contradictory that someone can be considered an example within a church while in their daily life neglecting such important responsibilities as those they have with their own family.

one_star_reviews.text: Yesterday I called to schedule a service appointment at the Tomares garage, mentioning that I had a "free" water and air filter change because I had taken advantage of a promotion last year offering two changes at a better price. Today, I arrived at 7:30 a.m. after asking my father to get up early to look after my children and my husband to pick me up, and they told me I couldn't have the service done there, that it had to be in Sueminencia. They said that if I paid for it, I could go because of some story they tried to tell me about warranties, but since I had the promotion (which I had previously communicated by phone), I had to go to Sueminencia. I woke up at 6:30 a.m. to get everything ready at home and be there on time at 7:30. Seriously, did nobody call me all day yesterday to change my appointment to Sueminencia? Not to mention that they made me take my car to the garage after I'd been at the office, only to then tell me they wouldn't take it. I can't imagine worse service.

one_star_reviews.text: Living near them is a real nightmare. The stench of manure, fertilizer, or whatever it is they use is so cruel and unbearable. As a company, it's deplorable that they don't care at all that those of us who live so close can't comfortably enjoy airing out our homes or having a coffee in the garden. In fact, even with the windows closed, this foul odor lingers so strongly in the air that you can smell it inside your house. A truly awful experience.

One star because I can't give less...
A DISGRACE 😡 🤦
I've lived in Riopark for 15 years and we've never had this situation before!!!!
You can't hang your laundry in your garden because it smells like manure, you can't swim in your own pool because it smells like manure and you get bitten by the flies... this company is affecting the entire community. WE CAN'T LIVE IN OUR OWN HOMES!!!

And what about... sleeping with a window open to let in the cool night air... when your whole house smells like pure, unadulterated manure... mountains and mountains of manure just 50 meters from your house 🏡

This company presents itself on its website as a high-quality farm with a good relationship with the neighbors, but the reality we residents experience is very different.

The constant piles of manure generate a very strong odor that affects the entire residential area, especially when it's hot. It's a very unpleasant situation that directly impacts the quality of life of those of us who live here.

Furthermore, I understand that the local councils have already contacted the company about this problem, but to this day, we're still practically in the same situation, with accumulations of manure and the same odor problems.

It would be appreciated if the company would take responsibility, implement effective measures, and demonstrate this supposed good relationship with the neighbors through its actions. Agricultural activity is perfectly respectable, but so is the right of residents to live without constantly enduring these smells.

one_star_reviews.text:
I WAS CHARGED 20 CENTS FOR A PACKAGE. AWFUL PICKUP POINT.

I don't usually write bad reviews, but after the treatment I received, I think it's important to warn others.

I normally choose pickup points because I prefer to support small businesses and also make the delivery driver's job easier. This time, I picked up two packages there. When I collected one of them, the person who helped me told me I had to pay 20 cents because, according to her, she hadn't made that 20 cent profit on my package (I don't know why).

I didn't have any cash on me, and honestly, I wouldn't have minded giving it to her, even more, because I completely understand that businesses make a small profit from handling packages. The problem was the rude and unpleasant way she treated me, even going so far as to ask me for a 20-cent Bizum payment.

If there had been a real cost or some reason that justified that amount, I would have understood without a problem. But the situation, and especially the treatment I received, seemed completely unnecessary and left much to be desired in terms of customer service.

For my part, I will not be buying or dropping off packages there again, and I certainly will not recommend this collection point.

one_star_reviews.text: Honestly, one star is enough to justify this review. You may be going through a rough patch as a bank manager, but that doesn't give you the right to interfere in the personal affairs of potential clients. Asking for a mortgage doesn't give you the right to say that marriages end, that people get divorced, and then calling the male account holder without the female account holder coming in to tell him you're denying the mortgage two days after he said he'd submit the documentation for the IVF (Valencian Institute of Finance) and the subsequent FEIN (European Standardized Information Form). We requested to be removed from the platform, and nothing has happened; we're still not listed. We asked for an explanation, and from this woman, we've only received evasive answers and then complete silence. There are banks like this, I guess. I don't recommend it. They pressure you into buying products that, when you add them up, are completely absurd. Using purely personal criteria instead of ethics and professionalism goes against the very nature of the institution, and running it like your personal fiefdom is even worse. Zero recommendation.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm giving one star because I can't write a review without giving at least one. The room was filthy. They gave it to us without cleaning it at all. The room with the coffin had dried flowers on the floor, and the family room had used tissue packets on the sofas, hair everywhere, and to top it all off, when we went down to complain, they told us the cleaner wouldn't come until 7:00 AM. And they didn't move us to another room.
It was a disaster, and the person at reception left much to be desired, being confrontational and shameless with the family members. A nephew had to stop him because he was being rude to a 76-year-old woman. The body is still there, and when we return, we will file a formal complaint.

The embalming service was awful. They left my relative unrecognizable, making our day even worse than it already was. I can only think—and this is why I complained—that the funeral home and the embalmer were definitely an inexperienced intern doing their training. If you care about your loved one, I absolutely do not recommend this funeral home.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm giving one star because I can't write a review without giving at least one. The room was filthy. They gave it to us without cleaning it at all. The room with the coffin had dried flowers on the floor, and the family room had used tissue packets on the sofas, hair everywhere, and to top it all off, when we went down to complain, they told us the cleaner wouldn't come until 7:00 AM. And they didn't move us to another room.
It was a disaster, and the person at reception left much to be desired, being confrontational and shameless with the family members. A nephew had to stop him because he was being rude to a 76-year-old woman. The body is still there, and when we return, we will file a formal complaint.

The embalming service was awful. They left my relative unrecognizable, making our day even worse than it already was. I can only think—and this is why I complained—that the funeral home and the embalmer were definitely an inexperienced intern doing their training. If you care about your loved one, I absolutely do not recommend this funeral home.

one_star_reviews.text: We bought some earrings because my daughter had lost the screw back on a pair we had from El Corte Inglés. We only wanted the screw backs, and Encarna told us they didn't have screw backs for other brands, that they didn't work with the brand, and that we should hurry and put them back in because the piercing closes up quickly. So we asked if we should buy new ones from there or from your store, if they had replacement screw backs in case she lost them again, because they often do. She said yes, because she had lost them. But surprise, when we went there, it was quite busy, so we went with two shopping carts, and the store was packed. I'm not going in. My husband went in, and when it was his turn, they served him quickly (they didn't even try to check if they had them). They just said he had to bring the receipt for the reference number of our earring. They didn't want to bother looking into why a screw back costs around €15. She wasn't very friendly, by the way; she even questioned whether the earring was from there. Don't you know what products you sell? I wasn't asking for it for free. Anyway, my husband left, and seeing how she treated him, I went back inside. After walking around for a bit, I went back in to talk to her. There was no one else inside, and again she asked for the receipt because she didn't know the reference number. I replied that I hadn't brought it, and if I looked, I might have it saved. I told her that when her colleague sold me the earring, she said they had a spare, that I lived in the village and didn't want to go to Valencia. At that time, I already had an earring from another brand, but I bought it again from your store! My response was, "Don't worry, we'll buy another one, or I'll find a solution." But I was indignant when people treat you badly, and that's exactly what happened. €15 in a store in Valencia, where she told me it was an easy earring, just three screw-ons. Without telling her anything about what had happened in your store, I took the earring off, and now I see black in the middle. In short, a disastrous experience. We want to support the stores in our town, but it's difficult like this. We have to learn to treat people better! I know that working with the public isn't easy, but at no point did we disrespect anyone, even if it was just looking for a €15 screw back for the earring we bought in your store previously. Besides, you don't know if that person might be a future customer! We won't be back, and your response that you didn't understand my complaint is something you won't understand! And no thanks, I won't be returning because you didn't even bother to look for the screw back for our earring, the service was completely unpleasant, and the gold earring in the middle has turned black, as you can see in the photo.

They played with our hopes.

We bought in November 2025 for €271,700 (including VAT).

How awful city councils are!

In May 2026, they canceled the reservation and suspended sales due to "the current situation of instability."

WE WERE LEFT WITHOUT OUR APARTMENT!

Surprisingly, in September 2026, they resumed selling the properties.

Great, in less than four months the instability was over!

The price of my apartment is now €329,780 (including VAT).

What a rip-off!

Blessed instability!

one_star_reviews.text:
VERY BAD EXPERIENCE WITH ABOGALEX / MIGUEL ÁNGEL NAVAS

I want to share my extremely negative experience with the law firm Abogalex and Miguel Ángel Navas. Unfortunately, trusting this firm was a huge disappointment, and in my case, the experience created far more problems than I expected to resolve.

From the beginning, I had the impression that I wasn't being treated as a client in need of legal assistance, but rather as a source of income. Before hiring them and making the payment, the communication was considerably better. However, after receiving the money, the attitude and quality of communication changed drastically.

During the process, I encountered a lack of transparency, poor communication, and difficulty obtaining clear answers about what actions had actually been taken in my case, what had been done specifically, and what I was paying for.

On several occasions, I had to insist to receive information and get answers to questions that I consider completely reasonable for any client paying for professional legal services.

What disappointed me most was the feeling of a lack of accountability and follow-up. When someone hires and pays a lawyer, they have the right to expect, at a minimum, professional treatment, clear information about the status of their case, adequate communication, and adherence to agreed-upon commitments.

In my case, I didn't feel I was receiving the professional support I expected. Instead of feeling that my case was being handled responsibly, I had to personally worry about obtaining information, reminding people of pending issues, and repeatedly requesting explanations.

I also have serious doubts regarding the financial aspects of the professional relationship. I believe there wasn't enough transparency about the services to be provided, their cost, and the work that was actually done. Therefore, I have significant doubts about whether the amount paid truly corresponded to the work performed.

For all these reasons, my assessment of the experience is extremely negative.

Furthermore, certain actions and circumstances made me feel that I was being provided with information in a way that could be misleading. From my perspective, the situation was serious enough for me to perceive it as dishonest and, in certain aspects, potentially fraudulent.

I want to make it clear that when I use terms like "fraudulent" or "deceptive," I am describing my perception and personal experience. I am not stating that there is a court ruling declaring that these individuals committed a crime. The final legal classification, of course, rests with the competent authorities and must be based on evidence.

Therefore, I recommend that anyone considering hiring this firm carefully read the contract before making any payment, request a detailed written breakdown of the services, fees, included actions, cancellation and refund policies, and the firm's specific obligations.

I also recommend keeping absolutely all documentation: contracts, invoices, payment receipts, emails, WhatsApp messages, and any other communication related to the matter.

In my personal experience, working with Abogalex / Miguel Ángel Navas was very disappointing.

Good afternoon,
On July 23rd, I went to the clinic after the pelvic adjustment by the osteopath, Vicente Pardo, on July 3rd, with the pain improving noticeably just with the right insole. Until July 23rd, when Juan Carlos fitted me with the two insoles, and in just one afternoon the intense pain in my left hip started again. Again, I called the day after the visit and they gave me an appointment for August 3rd (11 days later). They gave me a 0.1cm heel pad, which was practically nothing. They told me the pain would go away on its own, but it didn't, so I went back to Vicente Pardo on August 13th. He diagnosed and corrected the anterior and upward tilt of my right pelvis. How can you trust a tradesman who keeps telling you “it’s the company’s price” and acts as though he needs to speak to someone else to negotiate the price, when he is himself the owner?

What bothered us most was not only the price, but the way it was presented. As a foreign customer, I was left with the strong impression that I was being treated as an easy target who would simply accept an inflated price without questioning it.
If you are British, foreign, or simply unfamiliar with local prices, we strongly recommend getting several quotes before agreeing to anything. We certainly would not use his service again

A very negative experience with this clinic. Getting an appointment by phone is virtually impossible, and the online appointment system seems to exist only symbolically. They tell you there are no appointments available for a month, but when you go to the clinic in person, appointments somehow appear as available.

After the consultation, getting the prescription and test results became another problem. Despite requesting it several times, the reception staff were unable to properly email the documents. I finally had to pick up a printed prescription, and the test results ended up being sent to someone else's email address.

A complete lack of attention and interest in the patient, coupled with very poor organization. The reception staff demonstrate a worrying lack of qualifications and seem unable to properly use a computer or handle electronic documents. Resolving any simple issue becomes a lengthy process requiring multiple reminders. For a medical clinic, I consider this level of service absolutely unacceptable.
